acceptance_met: Fetch v8-17 positive response quotas mute new requests to only that broker. Fetch v4-7 retain server-side throttling, without a second client wait. Every completed response contributes its quota header even if the buffer budget discards its record body.

Already buffered records and unmuted brokers remain deliverable; muted partitions do not advance. Outstanding intervals survive socket replacement. Each interval starts at that peer RPC completion, so waiting for a slower peer cannot restart an expired quota.

All-muted waiting returns an empty batch at the poll long-poll budget, or Timeout at the earlier original request deadline. Connection and Fetch I/O consume the remaining request deadline. Wakeup and outer caller cancellation interrupt the wait, preserving positions and later one-shot poll settings.
ConsumerMetrics.throttle uses fixed-size saturating requested-duration counters from the shared tracker. Zero and negative durations cannot shorten a positive interval; no all-client quota claim.
